hook: Their bite cracks a palm nut human pliers cannot.
caption:
Their bite cracks a palm nut human pliers cannot.

The hyacinth macaw is the largest flying parrot on Earth, three feet from beak to tail, and its bite force can split the acuri palm nut, a fruit so dense that the only other animal in its range that can open one is the agouti rodent. The species depends on a single tree, the Manduvi, to nest in, hollowing cavities that take eighty years for the tree to grow large enough to shelter. Pet trade nearly erased it in the 1980s, dropping the wild population to fifteen hundred, and conservation nest-box programs have since pulled it back to roughly sixty-five hundred. The new threat is fire. The 2020 Pantanal wildfires burned thirty percent of its remaining habitat, and Brazilian state policy continues to authorize the conversion of Cerrado tablelands to soy and cattle pasture.
